reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every real inner-product space E with its normed additive-group structure, any functions g,p:E->E and any real eta>=0, suppose that g is monotone in the precise sense
  <g(x)-g(y),x-y> >= 0 for every x,y in E,
and that
  p(y)+eta g(p(y))=y for every y in E.
Then p is nonexpansive: for every u,v in E,
  ||p(u)-p(v)|| <= ||u-v||.
The conclusion is LipschitzWith 1 p in the norm-induced metric on E. The theorem assumes that a global p satisfying the equation has been supplied; it does not assert existence of such a p. It imposes no completeness, finite-dimensionality, measurable-space, smoothness, gradient, strong-monotonicity, or strictly positive eta requirement.
objects: A real inner-product space E; arbitrary functions g and p; nonnegative real eta; monotonicity inner products and the global implicit equation; norm-induced Lipschitz/nonexpansiveness condition on p.
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup and InnerProductSpace R structures. g,p:E->E and eta in R. The norm and inner product are those supplied by E. No completeness, finite dimension or measurable structure is required. There are no probability measures or finite-node arrays in the statement.
quantifiers: For every such E,g,p,eta with eta>=0, if the monotonicity inequality holds for every x,y in E and the implicit equation holds for every y in E, then p is 1-Lipschitz globally. Equivalently the conclusion quantifies every pair of inputs u,v. All p,g are input data; no function is existentially produced.
assumptions: eta>=0; <g(x)-g(y),x-y>>=0 for all x,y; p(y)+eta g(p(y))=y for all y. Only the stated real inner-product and normed-additive-group structures are needed. eta=0 is allowed and neither differentiability nor continuity of g is assumed.
conclusion: LipschitzWith 1 p, namely ||p(u)-p(v)||<=||u-v|| for all u,v in E. This is a norm-distance bound for the given implicit-equation map.
scopes: The monotonicity and implicit equation are global on E; the conclusion is global nonexpansiveness. The theorem does not establish existence of the implicit-equation map, a probability-kernel property, a transport bound, or a stricter contraction factor. Extra approved context about finite interpolation arrays is not part of this theorem. No material ambiguity is present.
constant_dependencies: The exact Lipschitz constant is 1, uniformly over all nonnegative eta and all g,p satisfying the hypotheses. No dimension, curvature, regularity or quantitative monotonicity constant occurs.
